name: normalize_signed_long_value
description: Normalises the signed 32-bit value in D6: a negative value is negated and its sign recorded, small magnitudes have their two 16-bit halves swapped, and the value is then doubled until its top bit is set. The shift count, kept in a 16-bit register, is decremented on each doubling and the routine stops early on reaching the sign bit or when the count runs out.

name: return_minus_one_status
description: Entry point of the library file that loads minus one into D0 and returns, doing no other work.

name: increment_count_clear_flag
description: Adds one to a 16-bit counter at a fixed offset from the structure pointer in A6, then clears bit 3 of a flags byte at another offset in the same structure. It returns no value.

name: decrement_count_release_if_flagged
description: Subtracts one from a 16-bit count in the structure. When the count reaches zero and bit 3 of the flags byte is set, it calls another library routine and returns that result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: unlink_node_or_mark_pending
description: Tests a 16-bit field in the structure. When it is zero, it reads a result field, unlinks the structure from its neighbours in a doubly linked list, calls a system library routine and returns the result. Otherwise it sets bit 3 of the flags byte and returns zero.

name: set_flag_bit_return_zero
description: Sets bit 3 of a flags byte in the structure addressed by A6 and returns zero in D0. It does not change anything else.

name: store_result_or_alert
description: Stores two input values in the structure and calls a library routine whose result it keeps in the structure. A zero result triggers an alert through a stored function pointer; a non-zero result copies the two saved values into two global variables.

name: copy_two_longs_to_globals
description: Copies two 32-bit values from fixed offsets of a structure addressed by A2 into two global variables. It returns no value.

name: tail_jump_to_library_routine
description: Jumps straight to one other library routine, which does all the work; it adds nothing of its own.

name: tail_jump_to_library_routine
description: Jumps straight to one other library routine, which does all the work; it adds nothing of its own.

name: store_value_in_returned_record
description: Calls a routine through a table in the structure given as its first argument, passing that argument, then stores its second argument as a 32-bit value at a fixed offset in the pointer that call returns. It returns no value.

name: chain_calls_release_on_failure
description: Calls one routine to obtain a value, then passes that value to a second routine. If the second call fails it passes the value to a third routine and returns zero; otherwise it returns the value.

name: load_header_into_record
description: Obtains a record from one routine and reads a second routine's output into a stack buffer. On success it copies a block of ten longwords and several fields from that buffer into the record, and links the record into a parent when one is set; if the buffer read fails it passes the record to another routine and returns zero.

name: copy_buffer_fields_into_record
description: Copies ten longwords from a buffer addressed through A6 into the record in A2, then copies several more fields from the same buffer into fixed positions in the record. If a link field in the record is set, it stores the record pointer into the linked record. It returns no value.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does no work and returns zero in D0. It only supplies a zero result to callers.

name: build_stack_header_and_forward
description: Builds a header on the stack from a fixed 16-bit tag and the value one, copies ten longwords and several fields from the record into it, then passes the header with two arguments to another routine. It returns no value.

name: read_icon_header_and_sections
description: Reads the structure of an icon file: it builds a path using the .info suffix, checks a 16-bit magic word and a version of one, then loads the optional sections and per-entry data into newly allocated memory. It returns one when the whole structure loads and zero otherwise.

name: read_icon_sections_from_registers
description: Performs the same magic and version check and section loading as the full icon reader, but takes its record, callback and output pointers from address registers instead of arguments. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: load_remaining_icon_sections
description: Continues the icon loading sequence: it stores two values from a read into the record, then loads optional pointer tables or further blocks depending on which fields are set. It returns one when every requested section loads and zero on any failure.

name: load_pointer_table_entries
description: Loops over a count kept in the caller's frame, reading one 32-bit entry per pass through a routine and storing each result in a pointer array. It then optionally loads one more pointer-sized block into the record, returning one on success and zero when any read fails.

name: forward_call_return_zero
description: Calls one other library routine, discards its result and returns zero.

name: return_without_work

name: emit_icon_sections_with_lengths
description: Allocates a 260-byte work buffer and writes an icon's optional sections in order, computing a length word and writing it just before each block. It returns one on success and zero on failure, freeing the buffer and restoring a saved field before it returns.

name: emit_icon_sections_from_registers
description: Writes the same section sequence as the buffer-based writer, but takes its inputs from address registers and allocates no work buffer. It restores a saved field before returning its success flag.

name: emit_optional_sections_with_lengths
description: Writes the optional sections of an icon, each block preceded by a computed length, including a null-terminated table of pointers. It returns a success flag and restores a saved field before returning.

name: emit_table_entries_then_block
description: Walks a pointer table in the structure, writing the length and value of each entry through two routines, then writes the optional secondary entry. It returns one on success and zero on failure, restoring a saved field before it returns.

name: emit_null_terminated_table_entries
description: Walks a null-terminated table of pointers, writing a length word and each entry through two callbacks, then writes an optional secondary entry. It returns one on success and zero when any step fails, restoring a saved field before it returns.

name: process_linked_list_nodes
description: Walks a linked list from the node after the header until it returns to the header sentinel, passing each node to another routine. It also passes the last value it obtained to that routine when that value is non-zero.

name: walk_node_list_until_end
description: Walks a chain of nodes starting from the value in D0, passing each node to one routine and fetching the next node from another. It stops when no next node is returned or the chain reaches its head, then passes any non-zero last node to the first routine.

name: forward_call_with_offset_pointer
description: Passes its first argument and a pointer 140 bytes further into the structure to another routine, then returns. It does nothing else.

name: allocate_and_init_record
description: Allocates a 168-byte memory block, calls one routine on one of its sub-fields and then another routine to set up the block. If the setup fails it frees the block and returns zero; otherwise it returns the block pointer.

name: store_pair_in_table_slot
description: Takes one slot from a counter, growing the table through a routine when no slots remain, then writes two 32-bit values into the next eight-byte entry of the table. It returns one on success and zero when growing fails.

name: decrement_counter_store_pair
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter through a pointer, then writes two 32-bit values from registers into the table entry selected by the new counter value. It returns one.

name: allocate_and_init_block
description: Allocates a 94-byte block and calls one routine on a sub-field, then another routine to set the block up. If setup fails it frees the block; if the final step fails it releases the sub-object. It returns zero on failure and the block pointer on success.

name: forward_call_with_offset_pointer
description: Passes its first argument and a pointer 78 bytes further into the structure to another routine, then returns. It does nothing else.

name: find_text_after_equals_sign
description: Scans a null-terminated list of entries, testing each one with a routine, and returns a pointer to the text after an equals sign in the entry that passes. It returns zero when no entry passes.

name: find_text_after_equals_sign
description: Scans a null-terminated list of entries, testing each one with a routine, and returns a pointer to the text after an equals sign in the entry that passes. It returns zero when the list ends without a match.

name: find_text_after_equals_sign

name: find_text_after_equals_sign

name: find_matching_separated_field
description: Walks the fields of a string separated by a fixed separator character, comparing each field's length with a reference length and then testing the field with a routine. It returns one when a field passes and zero when the fields run out.

name: scan_separated_fields_for_match
description: Walks the fields of a string separated by a fixed separator character, comparing each field's length with a reference length and then testing the field with a routine. It returns one when a field passes and zero when the fields run out.

name: parse_copy_prefix_name
description: Reads a name that may begin with a copy prefix and takes the copy number from the digits after it. It then writes the base name into a 30-byte field of the structure, formatting the copy index as the number plus one; a name without the prefix is copied as the first copy.

name: parse_decimal_copy_number
description: Checks a three-character prefix, then reads a decimal copy number from the text after it. It finishes through two routines whether or not the number was valid, and returns no value.

name: parse_decimal_until_marker
description: Reads decimal digits from the text until a non-digit is reached, then checks the four characters that follow for a marker. It finishes through two routines in either case and returns no value.

name: parse_decimal_copy_count
description: Accumulates decimal digits from the text into a count, stopping at the first non-digit, then checks the marker text that follows. It finishes through two routines in either case.

name: convert_decimal_digit_char
description: Returns the numeric value of a character when it is an ASCII decimal digit, and minus one for any other character.

name: return_minus_one_status
description: Entry point that loads minus one into D0 and returns, doing no other work.

name: call_library_slot_void
description: Calls an entry in a library table through a fixed offset from a global base pointer and returns no value. The routine it calls is not visible in this code.

name: call_library_slot_void

name: allocate_block_with_count_ten
description: Allocates a 96-byte block, sets a 16-bit field inside it, stores ten in a 16-bit value through the caller's pointer, and then calls a routine to initialise the block. It returns true when the allocation succeeds.

name: return_zero_stub

name: verify_call_result_equals_count
description: Calls one library routine with three arguments and returns its result when that result equals the last argument; otherwise it returns zero.

name: verify_call_result_equals_count
description: Calls one library routine with three arguments and returns its result when that result equals the last argument; otherwise it returns zero.

name: divide_long_by_word
description: Divides the 32-bit dividend in D1 by the divisor in D2 and returns the remainder and quotient as a 64-bit pair. Small divisors use direct 16-bit divisions, while larger divisors use a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract loop.

name: shift_subtract_divide_loop
description: Runs sixteen shift-and-subtract steps that divide the 32-bit value in D1 by the 16-bit divisor in D2, keeping the working quotient and remainder in local values. It returns no value and is the inner step used by the wider division routine.

name: multiply_low_32_bits
description: Multiplies the values in D0 and D1 using 16-bit partial products and returns the low 32 bits of the product as the high half of a 64-bit result. The low half is the value in D1 with its two words swapped.

name: call_format_library_routine
description: Calls a routine through a fixed offset from a global base pointer and returns no value. The table entry is identified by the executable's metadata as the system's formatted-output routine.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of D0 to the memory location addressed by A3 and returns.

name: count_c_string_length
description: Counts the characters before the zero terminator of a string and returns the count. The counter is 16 bits wide, so counting stops early if it wraps.

name: find_char_in_c_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for a given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or zero when the terminator comes first.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does no work and returns zero in D0. It only supplies a zero result to callers.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination, including the zero terminator, and returns no value.

name: append_c_string
description: Moves to the end of the destination string, then copies the source string onto it including its zero terminator. It returns no value.

name: strings_differ_within_limit
description: Compares two strings up to a length limit and returns one at the first differing character. It returns zero when the strings match through the limit or both end together.

name: return_one_stub
description: Does no work and returns one in D0. It only supplies a one result to callers.

name: walk_string_within_limit
description: Advances through a string, counting down a limit, until the zero terminator or the limit is reached. Only when the terminator is reached does it call another routine; it then returns with no value.

name: forward_library_call_void
description: Calls one other routine in this library and then returns. It does nothing else, so it only passes control onward to that routine.

name: copy_c_string_padded
description: Copies up to a given number of characters from the source string to the destination, stopping after the zero terminator, then pads the rest of the limit with zero bytes. It returns no value.

name: return_without_work
description: Contains no work and returns immediately without any result.

name: init_empty_list_header
description: Sets up a list header inside the block it is given. The first longword points to the tail slot four bytes further on, the tail is cleared, and the last longword points back to the header, matching an empty list layout.

name: validate_and_process_request
description: Returns one when given no request. Otherwise it reads a 20-byte record through one routine and, if that succeeds, runs two more routines and passes the field at offset 10 of the request to another routine, returning the final result. A failed read gives zero.

name: process_linked_entries_checked
description: Walks a linked list of entries, reading each entry's header through one routine and then processing its data block through another, with the size taken from a byte field. It returns one when the whole list is handled and zero if any step fails.

name: walk_entries_until_failure
description: Repeatedly runs two routines on each entry of a linked list, moving on through the link field. It returns one when the list ends with both checks passing, and zero at the first failure.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does no work and returns zero in D0. It only supplies a zero result to callers.

name: build_entry_from_stream
description: Allocates a 20-byte entry and fills it through two routines: one reads the entry's header, and the other reads a value and stores it in the entry's field at offset 10 before checking it. It returns the entry on success, minus one on failure, and zero when no entry was requested.

name: return_minus_one_status
description: Entry point that loads minus one into D0 and returns, doing no other work.

name: build_entry_list_from_count
description: Builds a chain of entries, one per pass, until the requested count runs out. Each entry is a 16-byte record linked to the previous one and given a data block sized from a byte field times four. It returns the first entry when the count is exhausted, or minus one when any step fails.

name: build_entry_chain_to_end
description: Builds a chain of entries using the same steps as the counted builder, stopping when an entry's link field is zero. It returns the first entry, or minus one when any step fails.

name: build_entry_chain_loop
description: Builds a chain of entries from a sequence of reads, linking each new entry to the previous one, and stops when an entry's link field is zero. It returns the first entry, or minus one when any step fails.

name: return_minus_one_status
description: Entry point that loads minus one into D0 and returns, doing no other work.

name: allocate_store_and_finish
description: Calls a library routine to allocate a block and, when one is obtained, stores the argument at offset 34 of the block and calls a second library routine on it. It returns true when the block was obtained.

name: allocate_store_and_finish
description: Calls a library routine to allocate a block and, when one is obtained, stores the argument at offset 34 of the block and calls a second library routine on it. It returns true when the block was obtained.

name: open_two_libraries_init_list
description: Opens two system libraries whose names the text references. When both open, it sets up an empty list header inside the structure and returns the structure. On any failure it passes the structure to library cleanup routines and returns zero.

name: close_library_free_structure
description: Closes a system library through a library routine, then frees the structure through the memory-free routine, and returns zero.

name: release_idle_font_entries
description: Walks a linked list of entries, unlinking each entry whose use count has dropped to zero, unloading its segment through a DOS routine, and reducing the structure's count for each one. When no entries remain in use it closes two libraries, frees the structure and returns a saved value; otherwise it sets a flag bit and returns zero.

name: close_libraries_free_when_idle
description: When no entries remain in use, closes two libraries, frees the structure and returns a saved value. Otherwise it sets a flag bit in the structure and returns zero.

name: set_flag_bit_return_zero
description: Sets the top bit of a flags byte in the structure and returns zero.

name: return_without_work
description: Contains no work and returns immediately without any result.

name: clear_flag_increment_count
description: Clears the top bit of a flags byte in the structure and increments a 16-bit count at another offset in it. It returns no value.

name: decrement_count_finish_if_flagged
description: Decrements the 16-bit count in the structure. When it reaches zero with the top flag bit set, it calls a library routine and returns that result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: collect_font_names_into_buffer
description: Fills a buffer with font entries: first from an in-memory list of names and attributes, then, when the file flag is set, from entries read off disk that carry a fixed header marker. Each entry is stored as a length-prefixed name followed by its attributes. It returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small, or zero when everything fitted.

name: collect_font_names_into_buffer
description: Fills a buffer with font entries: first from an in-memory list of names and attributes, then, when the file flag is set, from entries read off disk that carry a fixed header marker. Each entry is stored as a length-prefixed name followed by its attributes. It returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small, or zero when everything fitted.

name: collect_font_names_into_buffer
description: Fills a buffer with font entries: first from an in-memory list of names and attributes, then, when the file flag is set, from entries read off disk that carry a fixed header marker. Each entry is stored as a length-prefixed name followed by its attributes. It returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small, or zero when everything fitted.

name: scan_fonts_directory_into_buffer
description: Locks and examines the FONTS: directory on disk, copying each entry's name character by character into the output buffer along with its attributes. It walks the in-memory list of names as well, and returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small or zero when everything fitted.

name: collect_font_files_from_directory
description: Walks a directory listing, selecting names that contain a dot and end with the font suffix and whose header marker matches. It stores each selected name with its attributes in the output buffer, and returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small or zero when everything fitted.

name: store_font_directory_entries
description: Copies the names of matching font entries from a directory listing into the output buffer and records their attributes. It returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small, or zero when everything fitted.

name: read_font_file_entries
description: Reads a font file through a read routine into a block, copying name characters and the attributes of matching entries into the output buffer. It returns the shortfall when the buffer is too small, or zero when everything fitted.

name: scan_font_directory_with_cleanup
description: Walks a directory with examine-next and read calls, copying names and attributes of matching font entries into the output buffer. It releases its locks, file handles and memory through close, unlock and free routines before returning the shortfall, or zero when everything fitted.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does no work and returns zero in D0. It only supplies a zero result to callers.

name: score_font_match_distance
description: Compares two font descriptors by a size difference and by seven flag bits in each attribute byte, subtracting a weight from a running score for every mismatched flag. It returns a fixed large negative value when the first size is zero.

name: score_font_flag_mismatch
description: Starts from a size-based value and subtracts a weight for each mismatched bit across seven flag positions in two attribute bytes. It returns the resulting score.

name: score_font_flag_mismatch
description: Starts from a value taken from the flags of the descriptor and subtracts a weight for each mismatched bit across the flag positions in two attribute bytes. It returns the resulting score.

name: score_font_flag_mismatch
description: Starts from a value taken from the flags of the descriptor and subtracts a weight for each mismatched bit across the flag positions in two attribute bytes. It returns the resulting score.

name: return_fixed_sentinel_value
description: Returns the constant minus 32767 in D0 and reads no inputs.

name: select_best_scoring_font_entry
description: Looks for an in-memory font matching the requested descriptor. If none fits, it reads candidate font entries from disk, scores each one against the request, adds the best-scoring entry to the font list and returns that entry. It returns the entry it chose, or zero when nothing was chosen.

name: select_best_scoring_font_entry
description: Locks the FONTS: directory and reads its font file entries, repeatedly choosing the candidate that scores best against the request and adding it to the font list. It releases the directory locks and returns the last chosen entry.

name: select_best_scoring_font_entry
description: Reads candidate font entries from disk and repeatedly chooses the one that scores best against the request, adding each chosen entry to the font list. It releases its locks and file handles, then returns the last chosen entry.

name: add_best_scoring_font_entries
description: Repeatedly picks the highest-scoring candidate, adds it to the font list and moves on until no candidates remain. It returns the last chosen entry.

name: load_and_register_font_entries
description: Walks candidate font entries, choosing the best-scoring one on each pass, loading its segment with a DOS routine and registering it through the list-add and font-add routines. It uses directory-change routines around the work and returns the last chosen entry.

name: unload_and_add_best_entries
description: Repeatedly picks the highest-scoring candidate, unloads the segment of the previously chosen entry through a DOS routine, and adds the new entry to the font list. It releases directory locks and returns the last chosen entry.

name: add_best_entries_release_locks
description: Repeatedly picks the highest-scoring candidate and adds it to the font list. When finished it releases its directory locks and memory through close and free routines, then returns the last chosen entry.

name: build_font_file_table
description: Locks a directory named by the request and counts its entries that carry the .font suffix. It then allocates a table with one 260-byte record per entry, fills the records with names and attribute bytes from the matching files, and returns the table, or zero when any step fails.

name: build_disk_font_table
description: Scans a font directory, allocating a table with a header and a 16-bit count, then copies each matching font's name and metric bytes into the table. Only entries whose type code matches a fixed value are kept, and the table is returned, or zero if the load fails.

name: free_stack_slot_block
description: Passes the value stored four bytes below its argument, together with that slot's address, to a memory-free routine. It returns no value.

name: forbid_task_switching
description: Calls the system routine that disables task switching and returns no value.

name: permit_task_switching
description: Calls the system routine that re-enables task switching and returns no value.

name: allocate_memory_via_library
description: Calls the system memory-allocation routine through a fixed offset from a global base pointer. The result is left in D0 for the caller.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination, including the zero terminator, and returns no value.

name: seek_terminator_then_call
description: Advances to the zero terminator of the string and passes that position, with the second argument, to another routine. It returns no value.

name: seek_terminator_then_call
description: Advances to the zero terminator of the string in A0 and passes that pointer to another routine. It returns no value.

name: count_c_string_length
description: Counts the characters before the zero terminator of a string and returns the count.

name: accumulate_length_until_zero
description: Adds one to the value in D0 for each byte read from the string, including the zero terminator, and returns that total.

name: compare_c_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns zero when they are equal, minus one when the first string is smaller at the first difference, and one otherwise.

name: compare_c_strings_reversed
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns zero when they are equal, minus one when the second string is smaller at the first difference, and one otherwise.

name: compare_c_strings_reversed
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns zero when they are equal, minus one when the second string is smaller at the first difference, and one otherwise.

name: find_char_in_c_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for a given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or zero when the terminator comes first.

name: find_char_in_c_string
description: Scans forward from the pointer in A0 for the character in D0 and returns a pointer to the first match. It returns zero when the zero terminator comes first.

name: find_char_after_first_byte
description: Starts one byte past the pointer it is given and scans forward for the character in D0. It returns the position of the match, or zero if the zero terminator comes first.

name: find_last_char_in_string
description: Finds the last occurrence of a character in a string by measuring its length and scanning backward from the end. It returns the pointer to that character, or zero when it is not present.

name: find_last_char_in_string
description: Scans backward from the pointer in A0 toward a lower bound for the character in D2. It returns the position of the match, or zero when the bound is passed first.

name: find_last_char_in_string
description: Steps backward from the pointer in A0, checking each position against the character in D2. It returns the matching position, or zero when the lower bound is reached first.

name: skip_past_path_separator
description: Returns the position just after the first slash or colon in the string, or the original pointer when neither occurs.

name: increment_value_in_d0
description: Adds one to the value in D0 and returns it.

name: forward_library_call_void
description: Calls one other routine in this library and then returns. It does nothing else, so it only passes control onward to that routine.

name: forward_library_call_void
description: Calls one other routine in this library and then returns. It does nothing else, so it only passes control onward to that routine.

name: forward_library_call_void
description: Calls one other routine in this library and then returns. It does nothing else, so it only passes control onward to that routine.

name: forward_library_call_void
description: Calls one other routine in this library and then returns. It does nothing else, so it only passes control onward to that routine.

name: check_task_then_run_game
description: Game entry point. It looks up the current task and, when a field of that task is zero, disables task switching and records the result of a second call. It runs the main routine, then re-enables task switching if the flag was set and returns the main routine's result.

name: run_game_loop_with_scores
description: Reads or writes the high-score file in the S: directory through DOS calls, XOR-scrambling its 96-byte table with two fixed masks around the transfer. It then runs the main loop, which polls the fire buttons and keyboard, sets the display and DMA state and steps the game phases.

name: update_game_phase_state
description: Runs one step of the game's phase logic, chosen by a state variable. One phase clears per-object state and refills a table of tiles or sprites, while the other advances a timer and selects a tier from fixed thresholds, writing to custom chip registers along the way. The routine is truncated in the source bundle, so only this visible portion is described.

name: step_audio_nibble_table
description: Walks a table of bytes in groups of four, splitting each byte into high and low nibbles and accumulating them into two globals. It calls a routine whenever the accumulator is non-zero and sets the audio channel pointer registers as it goes.

name: copy_glyph_rows_to_planes
description: Draws text from an index table ending in a sentinel: for each entry it copies eight rows of glyph data into bitplane buffers, advancing by a fixed row stride. One buffer is always written, a second only when a flag bit in a global mode variable is set, and a third unless another flag bit is set.

name: manage_sound_channel_queue
description: Manages a software queue of sound samples across the four audio channels. It counts down per-channel timers, frees channels whose sample has finished, and when a request is pending it assigns a free channel, loading its sample pointer, length and period into the channel registers and enabling DMA for it.

name: manage_sound_channel_queue
description: Runs the same sound-channel queue update as the global-table version, but reads its channel table through address register A0. It loads the chosen channel's registers and enables DMA for it when a request is pending.

name: spawn_next_level_entry
description: Counts down a timer and, when it expires, reads the next code from a level table. Most codes fill a list entry with position, timing and pattern fields, a code of 16 resets the timer, and the end marker stops the routine. The table position advances with each code read.

name: draw_bob_descriptor_list
description: Walks a list of bob descriptors in a global table. For each one it programs the blitter's source, destination, mask and modulo registers, waits for the blitter to become idle, starts the blit, and marks the descriptor as done with a sentinel value.

name: configure_blitter_control_block
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then writes control words, masks and pointers into a block addressed by A0 to set up a copy. When a global flag is clear it also prepares a second configuration taken from a table indexed by a value derived from a global variable.

name: draw_icon_entries_and_ship
description: Walks a list of 10-byte entries and, for each active one, computes a byte offset from its coordinates. It shifts the entry's icon bytes into several bitplane buffers and sets collision flags where bits overlap. It then ORs three 32-bit masks for the player object into three bitplane buffers and their shadow bytes.

name: draw_scrolling_map_columns
description: Computes a fine-scroll mask from the horizontal position and stores it in a scroll variable. When a flag is clear, it programs the blitter for a copy and loops over twenty-one map columns, reading each entry's index and blitting the matching block.

name: update_four_effect_slots
description: Manages four slots of 10 bytes each. An empty slot is filled with a new entry at the player's position when a flag bit is set, and an active slot advances its frame index modulo sixteen, blits the matching frame from a table and adjusts its horizontal offset.

name: update_player_motion_state
description: Updates the player object's horizontal position, velocity and thrust from control flags, clamping each value. It then derives a map scroll offset and a frame index, and writes three words of output through the caller's pointer.

name: decode_joystick_input_flags
description: Reads a 16-bit input state word from the input record and decodes it into a direction code and a fire flag. It compares the result with the previous state and sets status bits when the direction or the fire state has changed.

name: handle_keypress_control_flags
description: Checks entries of a keypress table and sets action flags when a key is newly pressed, including fire, a facing toggle and pause. A counted special key spends one charge and calls another routine, while another key relocates the player, resets its velocity and adds a new list entry.

name: update_entry_counter_state
description: Updates a counter held in a list entry, selected by the index in D1. When the counter reaches its limit the entry is reset, and under flag and timer conditions a new list entry is created and another routine is called. Otherwise the entry's state values are advanced.

name: draw_masked_shape_to_planes
description: Draws a shape from a source table into three bitplane buffers, shifting each two-bit group into position and OR-ing it into two consecutive words per row. Positions outside the playfield bounds are skipped; the routine is cut short in the source bundle, so only the visible part is described.

name: update_drifting_point_entries
description: Updates ten drifting point entries. Each entry's position moves by a speed derived from the scroll difference; an entry that leaves its range is respawned from a seed variable, and otherwise it is XOR-plotted as a single bit into three bitplane buffers.

name: draw_counter_icon_below_six
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then, when the first counter is below six, sets up a blit of one icon. The icon's source is taken from a table offset by the counter value, and the blit is started with a fixed control word.

name: draw_counter_icon_to_five
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then, when the second counter is at most five, blits one icon. Its source is taken from a table offset by the counter value times 160, and the blit is started with a fixed control word.

name: blit_first_counter_icon
description: Blits one icon when the first counter is between one and five. It waits for the blitter to be idle, programs its control, mask and channel registers, sets the source pointer from a table offset by the counter value times two, and starts the blit.

name: blit_second_counter_icon
description: Blits one icon when the second counter is between one and five. It waits for the blitter, programs its registers, sets the source pointer from a table offset by the counter value times 160, and starts the blit.
